ben: Morning — quick async: kernel tuning pass landed on canary last night. Observed solid tail improvement but some microspikes under very small batches. TL;DR: 95p down ~12ms, 99p up ~6ms. Notes + action items below. ping @dmitri @carla for KV warming check.

carla: Nice. Can you paste the perf diffs? I also noticed eviction jitter on canary around 02:15 UTC.

ben: Perf summary snapshot: `bench/seq=256 batch=4` -> baseline 95p=45ms, canary 95p=33ms. 99p baseline=78ms -> canary=84ms. Kernel change was: prefetch throttle + slot-alignment tweak. Hypothesis: small spikes correlate with KV miss-rate >15% (see logs).

dmitri: On KV side — we bumped default TTL to 90s on canary to reduce churn; that might increase short-lived miss-rate for microbursts. I'll try rolling that back and rerunning the warmup.

carla: Can we add a short deploy warmup step? e.g. run a synthetic prefix load for 60s to populate KV right after canary spins up.

ben: Agreed. Proposed warmup command: `./warmup --seq 256 --qps 50 --duration 60` (synthetic prompts). I'll open a PR to add to rollout pipeline.

eva: :eyes: I added an alert for sudden 99p regressions to route to #eng-runtime oncall.

ben: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4727 — adds warmup step + metric tagging. PTAL @carla @dmitri

carla: LGTM, but add a rollback note — if warmup saturates tiny canary fleets we should abort and revert.

dmitri: I'll run the warmup locally against canary and post before/after miss-rate. If miss-rate drops <5% post-warmup we consider it stable.

ben: Blocker: seeing a flaky unit in `tests/batcher_test.py::test_slot_alignment` when slot-align enabled. CI flaky on macOS runner — suspect timer mock race. If you see flakes, ping me.

eva: I saw that too earlier. Any repro steps? I can take a look after this.

ben: Repro: `pytest tests/batcher_test.py::test_slot_alignment -k slow` — flaky on macOS. Suspect `time.sleep` coupling in harness.

carla: :thumbsup: I'll triage that test after standup.

dmitri: Quick Q — should warmup call `kv.prefetch` API directly or just issue real inference requests? Prefetch might be cheaper and faster.

ben: Good question. There is a prefetch endpoint: `POST /v1/prefetch` with body `{ "model": "rwd-7b", "prompts": [...] }`. Caveat: prefetch doesn't always populate dynamic per-prefix KV entries that the runtime generates on first inference; it primes shared embeddings/weights but not every KV key. For now keep warmup as real inference requests to ensure KV keys are generated. We can evaluate switching to prefetch for smaller fleets.

eva: I'll update the canary dashboard to show warmup vs baseline metrics for tonight's run and tag the graphs.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for `runtime@canary-20240215` — watching health checks.

ben: follow-ups: (1) dmitri to rerun warmup with TTL rollback and post results, (2) carla to add rollback note in PR, (3) ben to dig into flaky test, (4) eva to update dashboard/alerts. Thanks — ping here with quick results and I'll coordinate the canary window. :rocket:
